content: ⬛️ links and before we begin https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40) during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1) ⬛️ First things make the directory for UE5 and switch to it git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration) get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5 NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for cd /opt/hfsX source houdini_setup The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized. back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script] make (it shouldn’t require sudo) a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

⬛️ First things

  • git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git
  • now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh
  • then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration)

cd /opt/hfsX
source houdini_setup

  • back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script]
  • make (it shouldn’t require sudo)
  • a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors.
  • Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go!

While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

Trump Trading Patterns — Portfolio Dataset Data compiled for web-interactive visualization. All facts traceable to BBC’s April 2026 investigation, with corroborating sources where relevant.
Primary source: BBC investigation, April 2026 — “Is It Luck, Skill, or a Leak? BBC Probes Trades Before Trump’s Announcements”
Corroborating sources: Yahoo Finance, BusinessToday, NPR/AP, IBTimes UK (all April 2026)
Important sourcing note for your piece: The BBC did the primary investigation. Your piece visualizes their findings. Every caption/annotation on the interactive should credit the BBC. Language must match Verify house style: “the BBC investigation identified” / “reported pattern” / “alleged anomaly” — never assertive claims of insider trading, which is an unproven allegation.
Dataset: Seven Documented Incidents Incident 1 — S&P 500 “Liberation Day” Tariff Pause Field Value id sp500-liberation-day-2025 date 2025-04-09 announcement_time_bst ~18:37 BST (post-market interview release) announcement_time_gmt ~17:37 GMT instrument S&P 500 (tracked via SPY ETF options) market Options on S&P 500 index fund announcement_type Tariff policy (90-day “Liberation Day” pause) announcement_summary Trump announced 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs, excluding China pre_announcement_window ~37 minutes before reporter posted anomaly_description Over $2M wagered on S&P 500 rising despite 7 consecutive days of losses. Contract volume jumped from ~100s per minute earlier in day to 10,000+ per minute just after 18:00 BST wager_size_usd >2,000,000 volume_baseline_per_minute ~100-500 (earlier in day) volume_peak_per_minute >10,000 outcome_direction S&P 500 rose sharply after announcement primary_source BBC investigation, April 2026 notes Earliest of the BBC-reported incidents. Often cited as the most clear-cut volume-spike example Incident 2 — Oil Prices / CBS Interview “War Very Complete” Field Value id oil-cbs-interview-mar-2026 date 2026-03-09 announcement_time_et 15:16 Eastern Time announcement_time_gmt 19:16 GMT trade_time_gmt 18:29 GMT time_delta_minutes 47 minutes before reporter’s X post instrument Oil futures (short positions) market Oil futures contracts announcement_type Media interview — conflict status announcement_summary In CBS News phone interview, Trump said US-Israel-Iran war was “very complete, pretty much” pre_announcement_window 47 minutes anomaly_description Large volume of short bets on oil prices placed 47 minutes before CBS reporter posted about interview on X. Futures contracts betting on lower prices spiked more than 4x, fell, then rose again minutes after official announcement outcome_direction Oil prices dropped approximately 25% after announcement outcome_magnitude_pct -25 primary_source BBC investigation, April 2026 secondary_sources BusinessToday (2026-04-21), IBTimes UK (2026-04-21) analyst_quote Oil analyst told BBC the activity appeared “abnormal” Incident 3 — Oil Prices / Truth Social “Complete and Total Resolution” Field Value id oil-truthsocial-mar-2026 date 2026-03-23 announcement_time_note Time of Truth Social post (specific timestamp per BBC) trade_time_note 14 minutes before Truth Social post time_delta_minutes 14 instrument Oil futures market Oil futures contracts announcement_type Truth Social post — diplomatic status announcement_summary Trump posted that Washington had held “VERY GOOD AND PRODUCTIVE CONVERSATIONS” with Tehran over a “COMPLETE AND TOTAL RESOLUTION” to hostilities pre_announcement_window 14 minutes anomaly_description “Unusually high number” of bets on US oil prices placed 14 minutes before Trump’s Truth Social post price_before_usd <113 price_after_usd <100 (then recovered to ~104) outcome_direction Oil prices fell sharply, then partially recovered primary_source BBC investigation, April 2026 contextual_note Post came two days after Trump had threatened to “obliterate” Iran’s power plants, making the reversal newsworthy Incident 4 — Polymarket Cluster: US-Iran Strike (February 2026) Field Value id polymarket-iran-strike-feb-2026 date 2026-02 (cluster) resolution_date That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.

Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

  1. https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running
  2. https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735
  3. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40)
  4. during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE)
  5. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1)

⬛️ First things


  • make the directory for UE5 and switch to it
  • git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git
  • now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh
  • then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration)
  • get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5
  • NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for
cd /opt/hfsX
source houdini_setup
The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized.
  • back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script]
  • make (it shouldn’t require sudo)
  • a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors.
  • Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go!
  • after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now

⬛️ regarding updates and changes

soon(TM)

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/

content: ⬛️ links and before we begin https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40) during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1) ⬛️ First things make the directory for UE5 and switch to it git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration) get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5 NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for cd /opt/hfsX source houdini_setup The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized. back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script] make (it shouldn’t require sudo) a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:

So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:

content: ⬛️ links and before we begin https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40) during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1) ⬛️ First things make the directory for UE5 and switch to it git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration) get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5 NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for cd /opt/hfsX source houdini_setup The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized. back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script] make (it shouldn’t require sudo) a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

  • make (it shouldn’t require sudo)
  • a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors.
  • Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go!
  • after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now

content:
While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

content:
⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/
summary: lines of code / process for when trying to modify maps

content: ⬛️ links and before we begin https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40) during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1) ⬛️ First things make the directory for UE5 and switch to it git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration) get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5 NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for cd /opt/hfsX source houdini_setup The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized. back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script] make (it shouldn’t require sudo) a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

  • git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git

  • then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration)

cd /opt/hfsX
source houdini_setup

  • a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors.
  • Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go!
  • after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now
